top_stories.title: Microsoft 365 accounts compromised at 79 organizations, no passwords needed
top_stories.summary: An attacker compromised Microsoft 365 accounts at 79 organizations over ten weeks by replaying stolen authentication sessions, bypassing password-based controls entirely. Huntress tracked 497 successful sign-ins between July 14 and September 22, 2026, with sessions replayed from servers at 1337 Services GmbH, demonstrating a large-scale MFA-bypass attack via session token theft.

top_stories.title: 1Password for Agents lets personal AI agents log in without ever seeing the password
top_stories.summary: 1Password launched "1Password for Agents," a sign-in platform enabling personal AI agents from Meta, Anthropic, OpenAI, and xAI to authenticate without directly accessing passwords. The product addresses non-human identity (NHI) and machine authentication for AI agents, a growing challenge in IAM.

top_stories.title: AI-driven, large-scale nation-state campaign using ARTEX enables supply chain compromise
top_stories.summary: A nation-state threat actor, Storm-0940, used an agentic AI tool called ARTEX to conduct a large-scale supply chain compromise via ConnectWise. The attack involved application credential abuse targeting Microsoft 365 environments, directly impacting identity and access management across affected organizations.

top_stories.title: Trust Is Not What It Seems — And Fraudsters Are Counting on It
top_stories.summary: The article addresses how threat actors are bypassing traditional security controls by using AI-assisted social engineering tactics to manipulate help desks into granting unauthorized access. This attack vector directly targets identity verification and authentication processes at the human layer, circumventing MFA and other technical IAM controls.

top_stories.title: AI Agents as Insider Threats: Inside Microsoft's Bet on a Unified Security Stack
top_stories.summary: Microsoft has introduced Project Perception, which includes Guardian Agents designed to monitor and contain anomalous AI agent behavior within enterprise environments. Security experts are raising concerns that using AI agents to police other AI agents creates new insider threat vectors, with direct implications for identity and access governance of non-human identities.

news.title: You gave your AI agent access, but who is giving it orders?
news.summary: Gen Digital has introduced an Agent Trust Hub designed to address security risks posed by AI agents that can be manipulated into misusing their legitimate access permissions. The solution focuses on skill verification, secure connectivity, and runtime controls to intercept dangerous actions taken by AI agents through prompt injection via emails, websites, and plugins.

news.title: Hackers Breach Enterprise Firewalls and VPNs, Exposing Over 70,000 Credentials
news.summary: Hackers have breached enterprise firewalls and VPNs, including Fortinet FortiGate and Palo Alto Networks GlobalProtect devices, exposing over 70,000 credentials. The campaign targeted exposed network edge devices across numerous organizations worldwide, with operators attempting further compromise of some victims.

news.title: The AI Agent Nobody Owns: Watch Expert Webinar On Your Newest Insider Threat
news.summary: A webinar addresses the security risks posed by unmanaged AI agents operating within enterprise networks, focusing on their unsupervised access to API keys, database credentials, and internal systems. The content frames AI agents as an identity and access management problem, specifically around lack of ownership, access review, and oversight—core IAM governance concerns.

news.title: Machine speed attacks require machine speed detection and response
news.summary: Exaforce published an analysis of machine-speed cyberattacks involving stolen GitHub tokens, malicious AI installers, and MFA phishing, where attackers can exfiltrate data within minutes of credential theft. The report argues that automated detection and containment are necessary because traditional security team response times are insufficient against these attack velocities.

news.title: LiteLLM hit by second supply chain attack this year, users urged to rotate credentials
news.summary: LiteLLM suffered a second supply chain attack this year, with a malicious release pushed to PyPI and Docker registries designed to harvest cloud credentials, developer secrets, and AI service API keys. A previous March attack resulted in a 153GB stolen data archive linked to 2,488 corporate domains including AWS, Samsung, Cisco, and Salesforce.

news.title: eMudhra to Exit Global SSL/TLS Business After 8 Intermediate CA Keys Found Easily Guessable
news.summary: eMudhra, an Indian certificate authority, is exiting the global SSL/TLS certificate business after a researcher discovered that private keys for eight of its intermediate CA certificates were easily guessable and recoverable. The company's board made the decision five days after the vulnerability was reported, and eMudhra has committed to replacing affected customers' certificates with free ones from partners.

news.title: Railway Says Intruder May Have Accessed Customer Secrets, Urges Credential Rotation
news.summary: Railway, a Platform-as-a-Service provider, disclosed that an unauthorized third party may have accessed encrypted customer environment variables and in some cases obtained their decrypted contents. The company is urging credential rotation following the breach, which affected a subset of users whose stored secrets, such as API keys and passwords, may have been exposed.

news.title: OpenCode Flaw Lets Malicious MCP Servers Execute Code During Sign-In on Windows and WSL
news.summary: A vulnerability in the OpenCode AI coding agent allowed malicious MCP servers to execute arbitrary code on Windows or WSL systems during the user sign-in process. Anomaly patched the flaw in OpenCode version 1.18.33, with the code executing under the developer's own access privileges.

news.title: AGL hits half-million milestone with passkey adoption
news.summary: AGL has reached 500,000 passkey adoptions among its users, marking a significant milestone in its authentication modernization effort. The company discussed its technology stack and strategy for implementing passkey-based authentication as part of a broader authentication uplift initiative.

news.title: Keeper Security Launches AI-Powered Phishing Protection To Warn Users Before Entering Credentials on Fake Sites
news.summary: Keeper Security has launched an AI-powered phishing protection feature that detects look-alike domains, spoofed sites, and credential harvesting attempts before users enter passwords. The on-device AI capability is part of Keeper's zero-trust and zero-knowledge identity security platform.

news.title: authentik version/2026.8.5
news.summary: authentik has released version 2026.8.5 of its open-source identity provider and SSO platform. The release supports SAML, OAuth2/OIDC, LDAP, and RADIUS protocols for centralized authentication, authorization, and access management.

news.title: Enabling Passkeys Is Not the Same as Enforcing Them
news.summary: This article addresses the technical distinction between enabling and enforcing passkeys in Microsoft Entra ID, covering Conditional Access design and closing weak-fallback and device-code authentication gaps. It is part three of a seven-part series on migrating from MFA to passkeys in Microsoft Entra ID.

news.title: From buzzword to blueprint: Implementing zero trust on Red Hat OpenShift with the Layered Zero Trust Validated Pattern
news.summary: Red Hat has published part 4 of a series on implementing zero trust security within OpenShift using the Layered Zero Trust Validated Pattern. The article focuses on making zero trust implementation repeatable and structured within the OpenShift platform environment.

news.title: LiteLLM Compromised in Supply Chain Attack Delivering Credential Stealer and Backdoor
news.summary: The LiteLLM Python package (version 1.107.0) was compromised in a supply chain attack that delivered a credential stealer and backdoor via PyPI wheels and Docker images. The package has since been quarantined on PyPI, with the attack documented by security firms SafeDep, Socket, StepSecurity, and Upwind.

news.title: Best practices for integrating IAM Roles Anywhere with your PKI
news.summary: AWS IAM Roles Anywhere enables workloads outside of AWS to obtain temporary credentials by integrating with a Public Key Infrastructure (PKI). The article covers best practices for this integration, focusing on certificate-based authentication as a mechanism for secure, temporary credential issuance to non-AWS workloads.

news.title: Tech Giants Block eMudhra Certificates Tied to 8 Compromised Keys
news.summary: Major tech companies including Google, Mozilla, Apple, and the Go project blocked certificates from Indian Certificate Authority eMudhra after 8 cryptographic keys were found to be compromised. The affected certificates were revoked and blocked across browsers and platforms, though the cause of the key compromise has not been determined.

news.title: Close Identity Gaps in Software Development Before Unleashing AI
news.summary: A Dark Reading roundtable examined how AI is complicating identity security within the software development lifecycle. CISOs identified improved identity visibility and collaboration as key strategies for closing identity gaps introduced by AI-driven development.

news.title: ConnectWise Disables Cloud Backups Amid Concerns for Downstream MSPs
news.summary: ConnectWise disabled cloud backup functionality after researchers identified attackers authenticating into Microsoft 365 tenants using ConnectWise credentials. ConnectWise states customer impact remains unconfirmed while the incident raises concerns about credential-based access to downstream managed service provider environments.

news.title: BeyondTrust Remote Support Zero-Day Continues Trend of Exploited Edge Bugs
news.summary: BeyondTrust's Remote Support product was hit by a zero-day vulnerability, joining Ivanti, Cisco, and Palo Alto Networks in a wave of exploited edge device bugs. BeyondTrust is a privileged access management (PAM) vendor, making this directly relevant to IAM professionals relying on its remote support and privileged access infrastructure.

news.title: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 1,000 Security Holes
news.summary: Microsoft released a record-breaking patch batch addressing at least 974 security vulnerabilities across Windows and other software. AI is being credited for accelerating vulnerability discovery, though security experts note organizations are struggling to keep up with testing and deploying the volume of monthly patches.
